text:
jen-support: FYI customer is seeing sustained 502/504s hitting Hosted API via edge gateway when sending large embed batches (~50 docs). customer: @customer-jane. Request IDs: req=rc_9f3a, trace=tr_44b2. They're on standard tier, started ~10m ago.

customer-jane: Seeing ~40% of calls erroring with 502 or timing out after 15s. We tried smaller batch size and it improved. Can you advise? :sweat:

jen-support: Repro steps from customer (sanitized):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"embed-large-1","inputs":[...50 items...]}' 
```
They also attached an example response: `{"error":"upstream fetch failed","code":502}`.

nate-sre: Thanks, tagging in. Do we have edge metrics for 10:10-10:30 UTC? Any surge in connection errors or upstream timeouts?

ops-bot: alert: edge-gateway-502-rate spike detected on hostedapi-prod cluster at 2025-11-02T10:12:03Z. 1m error rate: 7.4% -> 18% for embedding route /v1/embeddings.

lucas-frontend: Noted pattern: large payloads + long upstream time (model runtime). Edge has connection pooling + h2 stream limits that can cause early resets under heavy concurrent streams.

alex-eng: Can customer try setting batch size to 16 and enable chunked uploads? Also want the exact client IPs and request headers for the failing requests (x-forwarded-for, x-request-id).

customer-jane: we can switch to batch=16 and test; attaching headers from one failing request: `x-request-id: rc_9f3a`, `x-forwarded-for: 54.23.11.9`, `content-length: 182345`.

maria-devex: Quick mitigation options: 1) advise customer to reduce batch size to 8-16, 2) add client-side retry with jitter/backoff, 3) route to dedicated capacity if sustained. We should also check upstream timeouts and pool exhaustion.

nate-sre: I'm pulling edge proxy histograms now. Early observation: h2 concurrent stream count per connection hit 100 on some frontdoors, and keepalive pool saturation + RST_STREAMs spiked. Suspect h2 window/stream exhaustion under large single payloads.

nate-sre: Can someone run a short tcpdump on frontdoor node fd-17 and collect Envoy logs for rc_9f3a spans? I want the upstream timing breakdowns: proxy_connect, proxy_write, upstream_response_time.

lucas-frontend: I can grab Envoy access log for that request id. Sample log line we see for rc_9f3a: `2025-11-02T10:12:08Z rc_9f3a 10.23.12.45:43872 - "POST /v1/embeddings" 502 UPSTREAM_RESET before_response_body - upstream_response_time=1.2s`.

alex-eng: That's interesting — upstream_response_time is short but we still see RSTs. Could be midproxy connection window thrash or client-side closing streams. Ask customer if they close connection early when they see partial payloads.

customer-jane: we keep connection open until response. No client-side aborts. We only see failures when batch >32.

nate-sre: Next steps: 1) collect pcap for fd-17 around 10:10-10:20, 2) capture Envoy admin metrics (active streams, connections), 3) try temporary increase of proxy h2 settings (max concurrent streams) in a canary to see if that reduces errors.

maria-devex: Also suggest they temporarily lower concurrency on their side while we triage. I'll send them a playbook snippet for retries + smaller batches.

jen-support: Customer agreed to batch=16 test. They reported after 8 minutes failure rate dropped to ~1.5%.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: rolling canary to bump edge h2 max_concurrent_streams on frontdoor-canary cluster started at 2025-11-02T10:30Z by @alex-eng.

alex-eng: Canary shows reduced RST_STREAMs on canary frontdoors, error rate for embeddings route dropped from 17% -> 3% on canary. Will schedule cluster-wide bump after validation.

nate-sre: Before wide rollout, we should verify no regressions for small-payload traffic. Also confirm connection pool behavior to upstreams (model servers) — we saw bursts of new upstream connections when large payloads hit. Might want to tune keepalive and initial window.

lucas-frontend: Added a dashboard panel for "h2_streams_per_conn" and "upstream_conn_open_rate" for embeddings route. Sharing link: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/edge/h2-streams (internal).

jen-support: Customer updated: batch=16 stable, will keep us posted. They asked if this will be a permanent change or if platform will better handle large batches soon.

alex-eng: Plan: 1) ship conservative h2 max_concurrent_streams bump to all frontdoors next week behind a feature flag, 2) improve pooling to upstream model servers, 3) add guidance to docs about recommended batch sizes per SKU.

maria-devex: I'll draft the public recommendation and a short runbook for support on how to triage similar cases (include curl repro, headers to capture, and quick mitigations).

jen-support: Thanks team — marking this customer as resolved for now. Will reopen if they see regressions. :thumbsup:

customer-jane: Thanks everyone, will report if anything pops up. Appreciate the fast help! :heart:
